strategies.overview: Entei acts as one of RU's deadliest wallbreakers, boasting a high Attack stat and an incredible STAB move in Sacred Fire. Sacred Fire's 50% burn chance lets Entei wear down even physically bulky checks, like Rhyperior and Gastrodon, as well as deter physically offensive Pokemon like Crawdaunt and Krookodile from switching in. Entei also has access to the coveted Extreme Speed, letting it revenge kill dangerous attackers like Mienshao and Armarouge. Additionally, its surprisingly solid bulk allows Entei to momentarily check the likes of Jirachi and Bisharp, allowing it to take a hit before eliminating them with Sacred Fire. However, Entei has middling and unreliable coverage, making it struggle against bulky Water-types like Suicune and Slowbro as well as Ground-types like Rhyperior and Quagsire if they do not mind getting burned. Entei is also highly vulnerable to entry hazards, particularly Stealth Rock; this forces it to choose between being able to switch in reliably with Heavy-Duty Boots or punching holes through teams with Choice Band. Entei's otherwise-solid Speed tier is rather crowded, causing it to Speed tie with threats like Mew and Flygon. Additionally, Entei is outsped by dangerous threats like Noivern and Gengar; the former can take even an Extreme Speed boosted by both Tera Normal and Choice Band and resists Sacred Fire, while the latter is flat-out immune to Extreme Speed.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

A Swagger set with Mirror Herb is an option to let Entei act as a setup sweeper, giving it immense power without locking it into a move like Choice Band. However, Swagger's lackluster accuracy and Entei's vulnerability to hazards in conjunction with its lack of immediate power makes it unreliable. Entei can utilize its surprisingly high Special Attack to run a set with Calm Mind, Protect, Substitute, and Lava Plume with Leftovers and Pressure, letting it PP stall foes while accruing boosts, though Entei's Stealth Rock weakness makes it rather inconsistent. Trailblaze can be used to get solid damage on Water- and Ground-types, like Gastrodon and Quagsire, in addition to letting it outrun threats like Gengar and Choice Scarf Gardevoir after one use. However, its low power makes it a poor coverage option outside of these situations. Tera Blast Grass is much stronger than Trailblaze, letting it take on the aforementioned Water- and Ground-types in addition to the likes of Rhyperior and Slowbro, though its reliance on Terastallization heavily reduces the flexibility of its team. Stomping Tantrum can be used over Stone Edge as a reliable coverage option against opposing Fire-types, like Armarouge and opposing Entei, as well as to dent Empoleon and Terrakion, though its lacking power compared to Stone Edge makes it less than ideal.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Because of Entei's lack of coverage against them, bulky Water-types like Slowbro, Quagsire, Gastrodon, and Suicune can stop Entei in its tracks and heavily dent it with their STAB moves. Offensive Water-types like Feraligatr, Basculegion-F, and Crawdaunt are capable of threatening Entei as well. All of them struggle to switch in to its moves, however: Feraligatr and Crawdaunt hate being burned by Sacred Fire, while Basculegion-F must be wary of Crunch.

Ground-types: Rhyperior, Gligar, and Flygon are all capable of taking hits from Entei before threatening it out with Earthquake. However, none of them enjoy being burned by Sacred Fire.

Fire-types: Bulky Fire-types like Talonflame, Armarouge, and Rotom-H can take Sacred Fire and wear it down with their secondary STAB moves, especially if Entei is Choice-locked into it. All of them must be wary of Stone Edge, however, and Armarouge's Weak Armor leaves it prone to being revenge killed by Extreme Speed.

Entry Hazards: Entei's pure Fire typing leaves it vulnerable to every entry hazard in the game, especially Stealth Rock. While Entei can run Heavy-Duty Boots to mitigate them, it is vulnerable to having them removed by Knock Off from Cyclizar or Hisuian Goodra as well as Trick from Gardevoir or Jirachi.

Faster Revenge Killers: Naturally faster Pokemon that can take an Extreme Speed, like Noivern, Terrakion, and Gengar, can KO Entei before it has a chance to act, especially if it has already been worn down. Additionally, Choice Scarf users like Krookodile and Basculegion-F can take an Extreme Speed while being able to get the jump on Entei.

movesets.name: All-Out Attacker
movesets.description:
Set Details

Entei is a phenomenal wallbreaker that can eviscerate common Pokemon like Bisharp, Jirachi, and Registeel. Extreme Speed is used to help Entei pick off faster Pokemon, such as weakened Noivern, Cyclizar, and Choice Scarf Krookodile. It's especially useful against more offensive teams, being able to revenge kill foes like Armarouge and Bisharp. Stone Edge hits targets such as Talonflame, Armarouge, and Noivern. Crunch is used to target Slowbro, which would otherwise come in comfortably. Double-Edge can be substituted for Crunch, granting Entei the opportunity to hit foes that resist its Fire-type STAB moves like Gastrodon, Suicune, and Cyclizar harder. Choice Band is usually preferred, as it gives Entei the opportunity to OHKO foes like Noivern with Stone Edge. Heavy-Duty Boots is good for teams that lack entry hazard removal, in exchange for being weaker than Choice Band. On Choice Band sets, Tera Normal boosts Extreme Speed to secure a 2HKO on faster foes like Noivern. Tera Normal also provides decent defensive utility, providing an immunity to Ghost-type STAB moves from the likes of Gengar and Mimikyu. Tera Normal grants Entei the opportunity to 2HKO targets such as Slowbro and Suicune, which would otherwise come in comfortably on Entei, with Choice Band-boosted Double-Edge. Tera Dark can also be used to further boost the power of Choice Band Entei's Crunch, being able to cleanly 2HKO maximum Defense Slowbro while also being able to OHKO Basculegion-F and Armarouge.

Entei is an excellent fit on balance and bulky offense teams, as they appreciate its ability to dispatch common threats, spread burns, and provide strong priority. Pokemon such as Krookodile and Bisharp appreciate Entei's ability to directly threaten bulky Pokemon such as Chesnaught and Registeel, in addition to possibly crippling Rhyperior with burn from Sacred Fire. This opens up teammates such as Choice Scarf Krookodile and Bisharp to sweep. In return, Krookodile sets Stealth Rock and utilizes Knock Off to help wear down Pokemon that like to come in on Entei, such as Slowbro, while Bisharp directly threatens Slowbro and can blow holes in the opposing team to allow Entei a clean sweep late-game. Bisharp has the ability to threaten faster Pokemon that Entei is vulnerable to like Gengar with its Sucker Punch. Special attackers like Gardevoir and Basculeigon-F pair well with Entei, as it can deal significant damage to their checks such as Hisuian Goodra and Empoleon. Choice Band Entei can struggle to get in if Stealth Rock is up, so it appreciates hazard removal from Pokemon such as Cyclizar and Noivern. In addition to this, Cyclizar brings Entei in safely against Pokemon that like to come in on it, such as Talonflame and Chesnaught, which Entei takes advantage of. Entei also appreciates entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Jirachi and Chesnaught. This helps weaken checks such as Slowbro and Rhyperior and weakens other Pokemon to be picked off with Extreme Speed. Jirachi also provides U-turn, which allows Entei to come in safely against foes such as Registeel.

strategies.outdated: This Pokemon was relevant in Regulation G, but has been banned in the curernt ruleset, Regulation H. However, Regulation G will be returning in January 2025, where this analysis will be relevant again. Additionally, the sets below have not been updated for Regulation G yet.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
• Access to strong priority and an ability that prevents Intimidate cycling give Entei a strong niche over other bulky Fire-types like Incineroar and Gouging Fire!

  • Sacred Fire: Sacred Fire's stupendous burn rate makes switching physical attackers into Entei a terrifyingly risky prospect!

  • Stone Edge: Despite its notorious reliability issues, Stone Edge is useful for being Entei's strongest attack against Dragonite and Terastallized Ogerpon-H.

  • Tera Blast Grass VS. Trailblaze: Tera Blast Grass has a chance of OHKOing offensive Primarina, OHKOes Swampert, and deals massive damage to Urshifu-R. Trailblaze misses out on these KOes, but the Speed boost can lead to easier sweeping late-game.

  • Bulldoze VS. Stomping Tantrum: Bulldoze is both a way to deal decent damage to opposing Fire-types and a useful support move with its Speed drop. Stomping Tantrum offers a bit more power and can match Sacred Fire in power if Entei misses an attack.

  • Crunch: Crunch is Entei's best coverage option for Latios and Latias.

Other Options
  • Iron Head: Iron Head does a bit of extra damage against Flutter Mane but has limited use otherwise.
EV Spreads

  • 148 HP / 244 Atk / 84 Def / 12 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread avoids an OHKO from Adamant Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch after Stealth Rock damage and a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball without Stealth Rock.

  • 132 HP / 228 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This spread spread lets Entei outspeed Iron Bundle after using Trailblaze or Bulldoze while only having a 2% chance of being 2HKOed by Choice Specs Timid Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • 196 HP / 132 Atk / 156 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This physically defensive spread survives Tera Dark Choice Band Adamant Chien-Pao's Crunch while still dodging a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball without Stealth Rock.

  • 116 HP / 116 Atk / 4 Def / 252 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This specially defensive spread dodges a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane even when with Stealth Rock!

  • 4 HP / 236 Atk / 4 Def / 76 SpD / 188 Spe with with Jolly: This speedy and frailer spread outspeeds all Landorus-T that lack Choice Scarf while still having enough special bulk to almost always avoid a 2HKO Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Entei's Fairy resistance is a big selling point as an Assault Vest Pokemon, but Terastallization can help with some of its poor matchups.

  • Grass: Tera Grass helps Entei with Water-types like Primarina and offensive Urshifu-R. Just note that Suicune and Bulk Up Urshifu-R avoid a 2HKO from Tera Blast.

  • Normal: While this Entei doesn't have enough firepower to sweep until late-game, boosting Extreme Speed is still helpful in this regard. It can also save Entei from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy isn't as helpful against bulky Water-types, but it makes Urshifu-S and Choice Band Chien-Pao much more manageable and surprises Gouging Fire that may attempt to set up with Breaking Swipe and Dragon Dance.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
• Being immune to Intimidate cycling and a better Speed stat make Entei a reasonable alternative to Choice Band Dragonite for priority cleaning.

  • Sacred Fire: Sacred Fire's horrifying coin-flip burn chances are a powerful deterrent to problematic foes like Urshifu-R, so it's preferred over Flare Blitz.

  • Stone Edge: As unreliable as Stone Edge can be, it's needed to do maximum damage to Dragonite.

  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze's Speed drop is useful for team support and 2HKOes most Focus Sash Flutter Mane, potentially saving Entei from a KO!

  • Crunch: Crunch deals massive damage to Latias, which can otherwise stall out Stone Edge with Recover.

EV Spreads

  • 116 HP / 252 Atk / 140 Spe with Adamant: This spread lets Entei outspeed up to Iron Bundle after using Bulldoze.

  • 148 HP / 252 Atk / 84 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This bulkier spread lets Entei survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: Entei can make use of its often overlooked Speed stat to outspeed Adamant Urshifu formes and Adamant Ogerpon formes, and it can even Speed tie with Chi-Yu.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Entei is a perfectly fine priority cleaner, but Terastallization makes that task much easier.

  • Normal: Tera Normal lets Entei do its best Dragonite impression, giving Extreme Speed such a boost that Chien-Pao can be OHKOed by it after Stealth Rock!

  • Grass: Tera Grass trades easier Extreme Speed sweeping for shredding through opposing bulky Water-types with Tera Blast, like Urshifu-R and Suicune.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• Entei is fast enough to be a surprisingly effective offensive Pokemon thanks to its immunity to Intimidate cycling and decent Speed.

  • Sacred Fire: Even though Flare Blitz is more powerful and doesn't contend with a irritating 5% chance to miss, the insane burn rate Sacred Fire provides is generally preferred.

  • Stone Edge: Stone Edge is Entei's best chance at breaking through Dragonite and Gouging Fire before without Terastallization.

  • Trailblaze VS. Grass Tera Blast: Trailblaze does decent damage to offensive Water-types and lets Entei outspeed the troublesome Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, but Tera Blast is needed to break through bulky Water-types like Suicune.

  • Swagger and Mirror Herb: This is the closest Entei gets to setting up, giving Entei the chance to pull off a shocking sweep and even be a nuisance with confusion! Outside of Swagger, Mirror Herb can be used for some risky switch-ins to punish setup moves with a boosted Extreme Speed.

  • Jolly VS. Adamant: Jolly Entei will outpace the prominent Urshifu-R, but Adamant is worth considering if using Tera Normal for easier priority sweeping.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 148 HP / 252 Atk / 84 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: If using Swagger, Mirror Herb, and Tera Normal, this bulkier EV spread can fit to avoid an OHKO from Adamant Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch after Stealth Rock.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Entei can function without Terastallization, but there are some matchups that will need it for.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is Entei's trump card against bulky Water-types like Suicune and Primarina and can save it from getting revenge killed by Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.

  • Normal: Tera Normal gives Entei a more late-game focus with Extreme Speed sweeping, especially if using Swagger.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy with Tera Blast is a less nerve-wracking way to deal with Dragon-types, with Roaring Moon particularly vulnerable to it.

strategies.overview:
• Entei is a strong offensive threat thanks to its amazing movepool, and access to Sacred Fire and Extreme Speed. Its great defensive stats combined with the immunity to Fake Out and Intimidate given by Inner Focus make it difficult to slow down. When next to Chien-Pao, it can threaten to OHKO on metagame staples Kingambit, Rillaboom, and frailer Flutter Mane sets.

  • As mentioned above, Chien-Pao is a great partner for Entei as Its Sword of Ruin ability helps Entei get KOs more easily. Chien-Pao can also remove Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain with Ice Spinner, allowing Entei to click Extreme Speed. Another great partner for Entei is Raging Bolt, which, with its powerful Electric-type moves, especially Thunderclap, can pressure foes resistant to Sacred Fire such as Urshifu-R. Ogerpon-W is also a great partner that can redirect Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes or threaten it with a strong Horn Leech.

  • Despite its strengths, Entei struggles against bulky Water- and Fire- types like Urshifu-R, Terastallized Ogerpon-W, Incineroar, and Gouging Fire, which resist Sacred Fire. All of them also either resist Chien-Pao's Ice-type STAB move or can mitigate it and Entei's damage output. Entei also faces issues against Farigiraf, which blocks Extreme Speed.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
• Snarl slows down strong special attackers such as Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Iron Crown. Tera Blast can be used instead when using Tera Grass to hit Water-types.

  • Assault Vest helps increase Entei's longevity against special attackers such as Flutter Mane, making Entei even harder to remove taking into account Sacred Fire's burn chance.

  • The EV spread allows Entei to survive a 116 Special Attack Modest Earth Power from Landorus and, when Terastallized, almost always survive Mystic Water Urshifu-R's Tera Water-boosted Surging Strikes, the rest of the EVs are used to maximize its damage output.

  • Tera Grass provides resistances to Water- and Ground- types like Urshifu-R and Landorus, as well as granting a Spore immunity. Tera Normal boosts Entei's Extreme Speed power while also removing its original weaknesses.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Entei fulfills the role of a powerful sweeper, using its high Attack in tandem with Choice Band and an Intimidate and Fake Out immunity to become a powerful offensive threat that can easily weaken or clean up teams with Extreme Speed and Sacred Fire. Flare Blitz can be used as a more powerful and accurate alternative to Sacred Fire, allowing Entei to OHKO Calyrex-I and defensive Flutter Mane. Its coverage includes Stomping Tantrum, which can help it hit Incineroar and Tera Fire Pokemon such as Calyrex-I whilst additionally allowing Entei to hit Electric-types such as Miraidon for heavy damage, and Stone Edge, which is used for hitting Flying-types such as Pelipper and threatening Fire-types, namely the Ground-neutral Ogerpon-H, whilst being naturally stronger then Stomping Tantrum. Choice Band bolsters Entei's physical power significantly, guaranteeing an OHKO on Calyrex-I with Sacred Fire in tandem with Chien-Pao's Sword of Ruin and giving Extreme Speed a high chance to OHKO defensively invested Chi-Yu when bolstered by Sword of Ruin and Tera Normal. The HP and Special Defense investment allows Entei to play more flexibly against special attackers, increasing its ability to take on the likes of Calyrex-S, most notably allowing it to always survive Astral Barrage from Choice Specs Calyrex-S and Electro Drift from Choice Specs Miraidon out of Electric Terrain. However, running maximum Attack investment allows Entei to maximize its damage output without hindering its natural bulk significantly. Tera Normal boosts Entei's Extreme Speed significantly, allowing it to pick up OHKOs on Tornadus and Landorus-I with Sword of Ruin and 2HKOs on Urshifu-R and Kyogre whilst providing defensive utility in removing Entei's weaknesses to Water-, Ground-, and Rock-type attacks, namely Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R, Earth Power from Landorus-I, and Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-C, and notably allowing it an immunity to Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S.

Entei, whilst being a powerful offensive threat, does struggle with many metagame threats, namely powerful Water-types in Urshifu-R and Kyogre, which can tank Entei's attacks easily and KO back; Raging Bolt, which can easily survive the majority of its moves and threaten back with heavy damage; and Landorus, which can threaten it with Ground-type STAB moves whilst utilizing Tera Ghost to avoid Extreme Speed. Additionally, Entei can struggle with being locked into moves by Choice Band, so foes like Incineroar and Pelipper and faster offensive Pokemon like Miraidon can take advantage of it being locked into its Fire-type STAB moves, whilst Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S can benefit if Entei locks into Extreme Speed. Additionally, Entei's reliance on a priority move for its damage output can lead to it struggling greatly against priority-blocking effects from the likes of Indeedee-F and Farigiraf. Entei partners particularly well with Chien-Pao, as it can assist Entei in wallbreaking through increasing Entei's damage output with Sword of Ruin and threaten the Ghost-types that can take advantage of Entei as well as Landorus, Miraidon, Farigiraf, and Indeedee-F, whilst Entei in turn threatens Chien-Pao's counters, namely Chi-Yu. Other great partners for Entei include Rillaboom, which provides Fake Out support for Entei whilst also providing Terrain control that can help against Miraidon and Indeedee-F, and Flutter Mane, which can control the speed of the battle and also threatens Miraidon, and both can threaten Entei's main answer in Urshifu-R. The Restricted Pokemon Entei is most commonly partnered with is Zamazenta-C, as Zamazenta-C threatens Entei's potential answers, such as Incineroar and Ogerpon-C, and Entei can chip some of its common checks, namely Landorus, whilst being able to threaten Ogerpon-H and Chi-Yu, which can assist Zamazenta-C greatly.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-7 points

Overview: Entei is a powerful physical attacker that can function as a wallbreaker and cleaner. Its spammable STAB move in Sacred Fire can be combined with coverage options such as Stone Edge and its strong priority move in Extreme Speed to wear down an opponent's team while using Inner Focus to block Intimidate. However, Entei has a fairly shallow movepool, a weakness to Stealth Rock, and mediocre special bulk. It also struggles without any physical setup moves to increase its Attack.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Using a Choice Band, Entei can use Sacred Fire and its limited coverage to deal large amounts of damage to the opposing team. It can revenge kill and clean using Extreme Speed.

Offensive Utility: Entei can forgo a Choice Band for another item, most commonly Heavy-Duty Boots. This makes it weaker, but it allows Entei to slot useful moves for the matchup, notably Will-O-Wisp and Trailblaze, which are both far worse on a Choice Band set.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Sacred Fire, Flare Blitz

Setup Moves: Agility, Trailblaze, Flame Charge

Utility Moves: Substitute, Will-O-Wisp, Roar

Coverage: Stomping Tantrum, Stone Edge, Iron Head, Crunch, Extreme Speed, Double-Edge

Niche Moves

Fire Spin: Entei can utilize Fire Spin against more passive foes, allowing for a favorable switch or a safe opportunity to set a Substitute.

Calm Mind: Entei can run a Calm Mind set to utilize a variety of special STAB attacks and its better special coverage such as Scorching Sands and Shadow Ball. However, these moves' lower Base Power and Entei's lower Special Attack make Calm Mind unappealing most of the time. It can occasionally utilize Roar to win a setup battle as well.

Solar Beam: Solar Beam in conjunction with Power Herb is Entei's only real way of hitting Water-types for strong super effective damage.

Eruption: Eruption is Entei's strongest special move, allowing it to compensate for its weaker Special Attack. However, Eruption is very inconsistent on Entei, as although it is fast, it still gets outsped by many foes. Entei's weakness to entry hazards also makes Eruption less viable in some situations.

Common Items

Choice Band: Choice Band enhances Entei's wallbreaking effectiveness, taking advantage of Sacred Fire's high power and burn chance to wear down Pokemon that resist it. Choice Band also increases Entei's ability to clean teams with Extreme Speed.

Heavy-Duty Boots: In games where Entei has sufficient power already, Heavy-Duty Boots can be a useful item to allow it more points of entry, especially if its teammates are lacking in entry hazard removal.

Niche Items

Damage-boosting Items: In matchups where Entei wants the freedom to change moves, it can utilize damage-boosting items such as Life Orb and Charcoal to enhance its wallbreaking potential while being more flexible.

Assault Vest: If you can ensure the removal of entry hazards on your side of the field, Assault Vest can help to shore up Entei's special bulk, allowing it to function more as a bulky attacker and as better support to its team defensively.

Leftovers: On a bulkier set and where entry hazards are likely to be absent, Entei can run Leftovers. This can allow it to use Substitute more, giving it more turns to safely use Sacred Fire.

Power Herb: Power Herb used in conjunction with Solar Beam is Entei's most effective way of breaking Water-types.

Tera

Entei is a fairly strong secondary Tera Captain, utilizing offensive Tera types such as Tera Fire and Normal to further enhance its wallbreaking potential. It can also use Tera types like Tera Grass, Fairy, and Electric to gain offensive coverage with Tera Blast to threaten Water-, Dragon-, and Rock-types. Due to its lack of setup options and reliable recovery, Entei cannot utilize defensive Tera types as well. It can perform well as a secondary Tera Captain, but there will be better options for your main Tera Captain.

Draft Strategy

As a mid-tier pick, Entei should not be a Pokemon your whole team is drafted around. It slots into some teams as an effective secondary threat, using Extreme Speed and Sacred Fire to wear down defensive foes and pick off weakened targets.

Entry Hazard Removal: Entei appreciates partners that can reliably remove entry hazards such as Iron Treads and Corviknight, allowing it to have more longevity and switch-in opportunities with its Choice Band sets.

Pivots: Entei appreciates pivots that allow it to find more entry points. It especially appreciates slow, bulky pivots that can take a hit and then switch out such as Galarian Slowking and Alomomola.

Entry Hazards: Entei appreciates having entry hazards set up for it, allowing it to further wear down its checks when they switch in. Reliable hazard setters such as Hisuian Samurott and Skarmory compliment Entei well in this regard.

Additional Wallbreaking: Due to its poor coverage, Entei struggles as a team's main wallbreaker. It appreciates wallbreaking teammates such as Urshifu-S and Dragonite that can assist it in breaking through defensive checks. Entei's late-game Extreme Speed cleaner sets also enjoy wallbreaking help.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Entei has no consistent way to hit bulky Water-types for any sort of damage, struggling against foes with reliable recovery like Alomomola, Milotic, and Vaporeon. They also do not mind being burned by Sacred Fire.

Entry Hazards: Entei struggles a lot against entry hazards, being weak to Stealth Rock and Spikes. They can wear it down quickly, limiting the amount of times a non-Heavy-Duty Boots variant of Entei can come in. In some matchups, Heavy-Duty Boots will essentially be forced, neutering a lot of Entei’s offensive capabilities with it missing out on a damage-boosting item.

Faster Attackers: Although Entei is fairly fast, a lot of foes will still outspeed it. Some of these offensive foes such as Landorus, Greninja, and Ogerpon-W can reliably check Entei by forcing it out and limiting its overall damage.

Ground- and Rock-types: Most Ground- and Rock-types have good enough bulk to switch into Sacred Fire and threaten Entei with their STAB attacks. They can hold a Lum Berry to mitigate the risk of burns.
